gen_risks.description: GORE Arequipa PIU lacks prior experience implementing World Bank-financed projects, creating operational risks regarding compliance with fiduciary, environmental, and social standards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide early targeted capacity building funded by the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) and mandate key staff appointments within 60 days of effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: GORE... does not have experience implementing WB-financed projects, so capacity building and close supervision will be required

gen_risks.description: Frequent climate hazards such as flooding, mudslides, and heavy rains could damage rural transport infrastructure and cause severe implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate-resilient engineering standards including slope stabilization, enhanced drainage systems, and resilient surface treatments into all road subprojects.
gen_risks.evidence: floods and resulting mudslides weaken transportation infrastructure, road closures impede access to tourism destinations

gen_risks.description: Institutional fragmentation across sector ministries and subnational entities could hinder decision-making and cross-sectoral investment coordination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalize inter-institutional governance mechanisms including a Project Steering Committee, Consultative Committee, and specific Interinstitutional Agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Efficient budgeting and implementation of investments in tourism are hindered by lack of coordination within a highly fragmented institutional landscape

gen_risks.description: Failure to sign at least three Interinstitutional Agreements with participating municipalities would trigger a disbursement condition delay for Components 1 and 2.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize early inter-agency negotiation and standard agreement drafting during the project launch and preparation phase.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawals shall be made... for Parts/components 1 and 2... until and unless the Bank has received at least three signed Interinstitutional Agreements

gen_risks.description: Delayed recruitment of key financial management and technical unit personnel could impede early project readiness and budget execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare standardized TORs early during project preparation and enforce strict legal covenants governing PIU staffing timelines.
gen_risks.evidence: Delayed recruitment of FM staff... To manage this risk, terms of reference for all the FM positions... will be prepared... in a timely manner

gen_risks.description: Initial delays in public budget allocation and low budget execution rates within the subnational system could negatively affect loan disbursement timelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate budget allocation procedures for external and counterpart funds in GORE Arequipa systems immediately upon loan signing.
gen_risks.evidence: In Peru, initial project implementation phases often experience delays in budget allocation and low budget execution rates

gen_risks.description: Inadequate familiarity with World Bank financial management guidelines could result in accounting errors, reporting delays, or improper SIAF transaction entries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Specify clear financial controls and FM procedures in the Project Operational Manual, supported by SIAF integration and independent annual audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Inadequate experience with Bank-financed projects may result in errors in financial records and reporting.

gen_risks.description: Elevated regional road fatality rates pose safety risks to tourists and local residents along rehabilitated transport corridors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate safety infrastructure including guardrails, road markings, speed calming measures, pedestrian crossings, and mandatory road safety audits in detailed engineering designs.
gen_risks.evidence: In 2024, Arequipa recorded 11.7 road traffic deaths per 100,000 people, a significantly higher rate than Peru's national average

gen_risks.description: Vulnerability of 17th to 19th-century historic churches to seismic damage and heavy rainfall risks structural collapse during restoration works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize traditional climate-resilient restoration techniques, structural reinforcement, improved storm drainage, and site-specific risk management manuals.
gen_risks.evidence: churches were built in the 17th to 19th centuries and are in various states of disrepair, many having suffered earthquake damage

gen_risks.description: High labor market informality and persistent gender gaps may limit female participation and employment benefits in local tourism initiatives.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct targeted capacity-building programs for female-led worker associations and execute a comprehensive SEA/SH Action Plan.
gen_risks.evidence: Peru also has a large gender wage gap... Measuring the impact of project interventions on jobs is difficult considering the high level of informality

gen_risks.description: Insufficient operation and maintenance (O&M) arrangements after completion could result in rapid physical degradation of improved roads and public tourism assets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear institutional asset-transfer protocols and formal O&M financing arrangements with receiving municipal authorities prior to contract sign-off.
gen_risks.evidence: the project will ensure that, once roads are completed, maintenance arrangements are put in place to ensure sustainability of the investments.

gen_risks.description: Subnational and national political instability could result in frequent administrative turnover and disrupt project steering continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Anchor project oversight in legally established steering structures with clear institutional mandates codified in the loan agreement.
gen_risks.evidence: The slowdown has revealed important structural challenges: low productivity and persistent spatial disparities, in addition to increased political instability in recent years.

gen_risks.description: Managing procurement across 33 subprojects spanning multiple technical sectors creates significant administrative complexity and potential procurement bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a tailored Project Procurement Strategy Document (PPSD) and reinforce procurement staffing within GORE's Logistics Office.
gen_risks.evidence: the project is an investment program, composed of 33 individual investment interventions in tourism, culture, transport, water/sanitation, health, and environment

gen_risks.description: Substantial environmental and social risks across multiple geographic sites could lead to local community grievances or operational disruptions if unmanaged.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), operationalize an accessible project-level Grievance Redress Mechanism, and enforce the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental and Social Risk Classification: Substantial

gt_risks.description: Peru is in a period of substantial political uncertainty (low popular support for the executive and Congress, high political fragmentation); a new government assumes office July 2026 and regional elections are scheduled October 2026. Since GORE Arequipa (a regional government) is the implementing agency, regional government changes could slow implementation or shift priorities; high-level changes at MINCETUR could also affect oversight commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Focus on highly needed, consensus-driven investments; maintain buy-in and continuous dialogue with the tourism private sector; engage proactively with any new authorities on project opportunities; use implementation arrangements that are technically strong, highly competent, and relatively shielded from political influence and staff turnover.

gt_risks.description: Tourism projects are inherently complex, involving infrastructure, capacity building, and multiple government levels/sectors plus private-sector and community stakeholders. Capacity must be built at GORE Arequipa given no precedent for multisectoral regional investment programs in Peru, and historic national-regional coordination weaknesses. The project also does not budget for O&M of delivered sites/infrastructure, which falls to designated stakeholders.
gt_risks.mitigation: Institutional capacity building via the Project (incl. GFPP) to ready GORE for implementation; World Bank support on PIU composition and key staff selection; coordination arrangements/agreements between the PIU and local partners in charge of operating sites, to align on design, implementation, and handover.

gt_risks.description: Combined fiduciary risk with GORE Arequipa is Substantial, reflecting the entity's lack of prior experience with World Bank or other MDB-financed operations in both financial management and procurement.
gt_risks.mitigation: A fiduciary assessment identified capacity gaps and informed mitigation measures; recruit dedicated FM and Procurement Specialists supported by qualified administrative staff; detail minimum FM/procurement procedures aligned with WB requirements in the Project Operational Manual; use SIAF for financial transactions/reporting and STEP for procurement planning/monitoring; targeted WB training, regular fiduciary supervision, and annual audits.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk reflects the scope/nature of planned interventions, works located in environmentally and culturally sensitive areas, and GORE Arequipa's limited institutional capacity to manage risks per the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthen PIU capacity to manage E&S risks with adequate resources/staffing; elaborate and implement project-level instruments (Stakeholder Engagement Plan, Labor Management Plan, SEA/SH Plan) plus intervention-level instruments with specific mitigation measures.
